heading: Observanda — a lab book for the curious
helpReopen: Without --workspace, reopen the last chosen location. With no saved location, start setup.
helpHeadless: --headless uses server-side folder navigation and does not launch a browser.
helpSetup: --setup opens the wizard without opening a workspace or changing saved preferences.
helpInit: For init, the workspace name is the folder name. An optional --title must match it exactly.
helpPreferences: --preferences selects the app preferences file; workspace files are stored separately.
helpDatabase: Without OBSERVANDA_DATABASE_URL, each workspace owns its private PostgreSQL database files.
helpRuntime: Windows downloads a checksum-pinned runtime; Linux/macOS use installed tools or apt/dnf/Homebrew.
helpMac: macOS also uses its system Perl for the database process lock.
helpInstall: Package managers may ask for system administrator permission. OBSERVANDA_POSTGRES_BIN selects existing tools.
helpExternalDatabase: Set OBSERVANDA_DATABASE_URL to use an organization-managed PostgreSQL database instead.
helpDatabaseAccess:
Use an ordinary database owner; a superuser is not required. For remote databases,
set OBSERVANDA_DATABASE_TLS=verify-full and optionally OBSERVANDA_DATABASE_CA to a CA certificate file.
helpCredentials:
Managed database credentials are encrypted with the workspace key. External connection credentials
stay in the service environment and are never included in portable workspace exports.
helpEncryption: New workspaces are always encrypted. Windows supports OS-protected device keys.
helpPassword: --password-stdin reads an encryption password from standard input for init, validate or build.
helpBuild: Build exports only entries explicitly selected for sharing. Existing output is never overwritten.
helpPublishing: No command creates a GitHub repository, commits, pushes, or publishes to a server.

browserAuthorization: To authorize a browser, open {file} in the browser-launch folder beside your preferences file within two minutes. The authorization can be used once.
